kept.claim: The org/team ANY(array) SQL is never executed against Postgres in tests and the caching tests were removed while caching code remains - a coverage gap, not a demonstrated bug.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Org/team raw SQL (`= ANY(array)`) is never executed in tests; caching tests removed

**Severity:** LOW — the riskiest new SQL has only string-shape assertions

### The Problem

The PR rewrites org and team authorization into raw SQL using array parameters:

```ts
Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`
Prisma.sql`("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)`
```

but the only test that actually runs a query (`getBaseConditions` test, line 480-484) uses `scope: "user"`, which produces `("userId" = $1) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)` — no arrays, no OR. The org/team tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` objects with `toEqual`, which proves the builder emits the text the test author expected, not that Postgres accepts it or that it returns the right rows. In addition, the whole `describe("Caching")` block was deleted although `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still cache.

### Theory / Proof

`toEqual` on two `Sql` instances compares their `strings`/`values` arrays; a column-name typo, wrong quoting, or an array-parameter type issue would be mirrored in the expectation and still pass. The PR description itself notes the author could not run the tests.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The shape assertions pass, and no failing path is known: `teamIds` always contains `orgId` (line 154) and the `userId = ANY(...)` clauses are only added when the array is non-empty, so empty-array edge cases are avoided. The caching logic is unchanged apart from its type. This is a coverage gap: a future regression in array binding or in how the OR fragment composes would only surface in production.

### Recommendation

Add an executed query for org and team scope, e.g.:

```ts
const service = new InsightsBookingService({ prisma, options: { scope: "org", userId: testData.user.id, orgId: testData.org.id } });
const base = await service.getBaseConditions();
const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw<{ id: number }[]>`
  SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${base}`;
expect(rows.map((r) => r.id)).toContain(testData.booking.id);
```

and restore the two caching tests (they only need their expectations changed to `Prisma.sql`).
